Encroachment density

Every 500 m of route, rated

The rating is a count rule that tells you where to send people first. It is not a safety or integrity assessment.

What a delivery contains

The same outputs, for your route

PDF report

A cover with the key figures; survey details (method, imagery source and date, UTM zone); an overview map with buffers, chainage and a scale bar; the segment table; a photo of each structure in chainage order; and the full coordinate register. In English or Portuguese.

GIS layers

GeoPackage, GeoJSON, KMZ and Shapefile. Each structure carries its distance to the line and its buffer band; the route is split into rated segments. They open in QGIS, ArcGIS and Google Earth.

Interactive map file

A self-contained map of the results that opens in a web browser. The result layers work offline; background imagery needs a connection unless your survey imagery is included.

About this sample

What this sample can and cannot show

  • Where structures stand relative to the line, by band and by stretch of route
  • How the density rating turns a register into a list of stretches to visit first
  • What your GIS team receives and how the files are structured
  • Who lives in a structure, who owns it, or what it is used for
  • Whether a structure is authorised: that is for the route owner and the authorities
  • Anything about the pipeline’s condition or integrity

Shown with permission

We never publish a client’s route, imagery or results without written permission. The T-9 route is shown here with the route owner’s permission. The facilities near both ends of the route are the operator’s own installations: they are part of the asset, not encroachment, and are not in the register.

Frequently asked questions

Is this sample automatic detection?

No. Every mark in this sample was placed by a reviewer on satellite imagery; no automatic detection result is shown. On a client survey, open building datasets and segmentation models propose structures first and a reviewer confirms, corrects and adds to them. See how we detect, review and measure structures.

Why is the imagery not dated?

This sample was reviewed on a Google satellite basemap, which does not state when its images were captured. That is fine for a sample and for internal screening, but not for a record that must reflect a date. Client surveys that need a date use dated imagery, such as a drone survey, a purchased satellite scene or your own georeferenced imagery.

Some structures on the imagery have no mark. Why?

The review recorded the structures the reviewer confirmed at the time, inside the search area around the route. Structures under tree cover, roofs that blend with the ground and anything outside the search area are not marked. A delivered survey is reviewed against the imagery it names, and anything that cannot be settled from the air is listed for a check on the ground.

Why are the boxes slightly off some roofs?

Reviewer marks are points. The boxes are drawn around each point so they can be seen at this scale, and a point placed at the edge of a roof puts its box partly on the ground next to it. Distances are measured from the point.

Are the plants and well pads on the route counted?

No. The facilities near both ends of this route belong to the pipeline operator. An operator’s own installations are part of the asset, not encroachment, and they are not in the register.
